top_signals.title: What Israel’s Election Results Mean for the Middle East and Beyond
top_signals.summary:
Israeli elections on Oct. 27 produced a complex result, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition alliance, led by Gadi Eisenkot, winning enough seats in the Knesset to form a government. The opposition faces a tricky choice: attempt to form a unity government with Netanyahu, after channeling anger at the prime minister during the campaign, or partner with the Israeli-Arab parties, which performed unusually well in the election. The latter option, however, is deeply unpalatable to most of the Jewish opposition. A period of negotiations now commences, while Netanyahu remains in a caretaker position. If no governing

top_signals.title: Treasuries Advance as Traders Eye US Votes, Refinancing Plans
top_signals.summary: US Treasuries gained across the curve ahead of the Treasury’s quarterly issuance plans, with traders reacting to the first vote counts from the midterm elections that favored the Democrats.

top_signals.title: Pentagon Eyes Unprecedented 75-Year Deal to End China's Rare Earth Stranglehold
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Army wants first dibs on American-produced heavy rare earths, and REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has just signed a landmark nonbinding term sheet that could put it at the top of the military's supply chain list. And the terms are extraordinary. The term sheet proposes a potential 75-year operating lease on approximately 200 acres at Tooele Army Depot in Utah, where REalloys would build and operate a facility processing dysprosium and terbium, two metals China has spent decades monopolizing. top_signals.title: US Stock Futures Drop as Democrats Gain Early Momentum in Vote
top_signals.summary: US stock futures extended losses as early midterm vote counts pointed to a strong Democratic showing, raising worries over tighter regulatory scrutiny in sectors that have powered a bull market on Wall Street.

top_signals.title: Stocks Drop With Dollar as Count Favors Democrats: Markets Wrap
top_signals.summary: US equity-index futures fell and the dollar weakened as early midterm vote counts and prediction markets pointed to rising chances of a Democratic victory, raising the prospect of gridlock in Washington. Treasuries gained.
